diagrams.title: Dermatomyositis Treatment by Active Domain
diagrams.subtitle: A multidisciplinary framework—not a substitute for patient-specific prescribing

foundation.text: Rigorous photoprotection; topical corticosteroid or calcineurin inhibitor; treat scalp scale/pruritus; document CDASI activity vs damage.
foundation.detail: Persistent erythema, scale, ulceration, or pruritus indicates activity; dyspigmentation, atrophy, and scarring may represent damage and will not respond like active inflammation.

steroid-sparing.text: Methotrexate or mycophenolate are common systemic choices; select by extracutaneous domains, pregnancy plans, laboratory profile, and comorbidity.

escalation.text: IVIG for refractory/severe disease. Brepocitinib 30 mg improved composite, skin, function, and glucocorticoid-taper outcomes in the phase 3 VALOR trial; as of 2026-08-03 its US NDA is under FDA Priority Review and it must not be represented as approved. Other targeted therapies remain specialist-directed and often off-label.
escalation.detail: Regulatory status is time-sensitive. Verify the current FDA label before prescribing. VALOR also reported more serious infections with brepocitinib 30 mg than placebo, so trial efficacy does not replace individualized safety assessment.

foundation.text: For clinically important weakness, systemic glucocorticoid is commonly used while rapidly excluding mimics and assessing swallowing/respiration.

steroid-sparing.text: Start an early steroid-sparing agent such as methotrexate, azathioprine, or mycophenolate; integrate physical therapy after acute safety assessment.

escalation.text: IVIG, rituximab, or other specialist-directed therapy for refractory or severe disease; use objective strength/function rather than CK alone.

foundation.text: Urgent swallow and nutrition assessment; aspiration precautions; evaluate respiratory complications.

steroid-sparing.text: Treat active myositis aggressively with systemic therapy; coordinate speech-language pathology and gastroenterology/ENT as needed.

escalation.text: IVIG is often prioritized in severe dysphagia; hospital-level care if aspiration, dehydration, or inability to maintain nutrition.

foundation.text: Pulmonology/rheumatology co-management; HRCT/PFT baseline; exclude infection and alternative causes.

steroid-sparing.text: Mycophenolate is commonly favored; rituximab, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, calcineurin inhibitor, or other agents depend on phenotype and severity.

escalation.text: Rapidly progressive ILD—especially MDA5—requires urgent combination therapy and respiratory support. Treatment choices should follow current SARD-ILD guidance and local expertise.

foundation.text: Control active inflammation early; minimize trauma; wound care and infection management; assess pain and function.

steroid-sparing.text: No uniformly effective medical therapy. Optimize underlying disease control and consider selected agents case by case.

escalation.text: Surgical removal may help discrete symptomatic lesions after inflammation is controlled; extensive disease needs multidisciplinary planning.

citations.quote: The ProDERM randomized trial demonstrated improvement with IVIG in active adult dermatomyositis and identified clinically important thromboembolic risk.
ACR/CHEST guideline provides disease-specific initial, progressive, and rapidly progressive SARD-ILD treatment frameworks.
Garg, Merola, and Fitzpatrick (eds.). Interdisciplinary Approaches to Overlap Disorders in Dermatology & Rheumatology. Springer, 2022.
VALOR found that brepocitinib 30 mg, but not 15 mg, improved the week-52 Total Improvement Score and all nine key secondary endpoints; serious infections were more frequent than with placebo.
Roivant reported on 2026-03-03 that FDA accepted the dermatomyositis NDA and granted Priority Review; the application remained under review at this audit date.
